fallback.text: The human beta-globin gene (HBB) starts ATG GTG CAT CTG ACT CCT GAG GAG …: codon 7 is GAG, glutamic acid (counted from the initiator methionine; the older count, which leaves the methionine out, calls it codon 6). Changing its middle base A to T (c.20A>T) turns GAG into GTG, valine: p.(Glu7Val), the sickle-cell mutation of haemoglobin S. It is a missense change between amino acids of opposite character (BLOSUM62 −2: a charged residue becomes a hydrophobic one on the protein's surface), and it removes the Bsu36I (MstII) site CCTNAGG at codons 6–8, which is how the allele used to be detected on a gel. The same codon changed to AAG gives lysine, haemoglobin C; changing its last base to A (GAA) is silent.
